docs.title: Your agents need your judgement
docs.text: Keeping up with their work takes attention. Spacedock brings plans and drafts to you for review. It helps you and your agents keep your goals on track, and lets you define which decisions need you.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Paste this into your agent:

Install Spacedock using https://spacedock.md/agents.md and use Spacedock Review for plans and artifacts I need to review. copy

Manual installation.

docs.title: Your attention bottlenecks
docs.text:
Your attention goes into judging work, keeping goals on track and setting the standards agents work to.

  • Review: Bring the work and evidence together when you need to make a call.
  • Compass: Check where your agents' work stands against your goals.
  • Workflow: Define what needs your judgement and refine it as trust grows.

docs.title: External trackers
docs.text:
Your backlog can stay in GitHub Issues, Linear or another tracker.

Ask your agent to create a workflow item from an external issue. For example: “Intake GitHub issue #134.”

The workflow item keeps a reference to the source. The tracker remains the place for intake and discussion; Spacedock coordinates execution.

docs.title: Mods and standing teammates
docs.text: A mod adds behavior to a workflow without adding a stage. Ask your agent to install an existing mod or create one.

docs.title: Lifecycle hooks
docs.text:
A mod can act at startup, while the workflow is idle or before work completes.

For example, the pr-merge mod manages pull requests and keeps work open until the PR merges.

docs.title: Standing teammates
docs.text:
A standing teammate is a specialist agent available throughout a session for recurring work.

For example, the comm-officer mod provides a prose editor for drafts and summaries.

docs.title: Multiple workflows
docs.text:
A project can have several workflows, each with its own stages and standards. Your agent can coordinate them in one session.

For example, one workflow can run experiments while another develops the software those experiments need.

Tell your agent about dependencies between work items so it can account for them before dispatch.

docs.title: Local plugin development
docs.text: For normal setup, use Installation.

docs.title: Local checkout
docs.text:
Use --plugin-dir <checkout> before -- to select a local plugin checkout.

For Claude Code and Pi, the override applies to that session and does not use the Safehouse sandbox.

For Codex, it creates a persistent installation that replaces the existing Spacedock plugin. Run the command again after changes to the checkout.

Codex does not accept --plugin-dir after --.

docs.title: Alternate marketplace
docs.text:
Set SPACEDOCK_MARKETPLACE_SOURCE to select a local or alternate marketplace:

SPACEDOCK_MARKETPLACE_SOURCE=/path/to/local/marketplace spacedock install --host codex

docs.title: Workflow refits
docs.text:
After a Spacedock upgrade, use /spacedock:refit path/to/workflow in Claude Code to update the generated workflow files.

Your agent presents a diff for each proposed change, including any migration. You decide what to apply.

docs.title: Split-root state
docs.text:
Split-root state keeps workflow progress commits off your code branch. Workflow rules stay with the code; work records live in a separate Git checkout.

Ask your agent to configure this layout. On a fresh clone, restore the state checkout with:

spacedock state init

Conflicting edits to the same work item stop for your decision.

docs.title: What is Spacedock Compass
docs.text: You give an agent a goal and go do something else. Twenty turns later it is rewriting a file you never mentioned, or it has declared the work done and it isn't. With several sessions running, you find out when you read the result. Compass keeps the goal you set beside what each session is doing, so the session that has left it stands out while it is still running.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Compass is a screen on your own machine that lists every agent session you have running, across Claude Code, Codex and eight other agent tools. For each active session it shows where the work is, what the agent is doing now, what it does next, and whether it is blocked.

Each active session shows its goal beside what the agent is doing. Sessions with a recorded departure carry a Drift mark and sit above ordinary working sessions, below sessions waiting on you or holding a question.

This is Intent and drift. You state your intent for a session as a goal. A /goal you set in Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity becomes the goal on its own. When you ask, Compass checks the session against that intent and says where the agent departed, citing the exact entries in the session record. When Claude Code or Codex says a goal is met, Compass displays the claim; Analyze drift checks it against what the session recorded. You decide what to do about a departure: tell the agent, adjust the intent, or leave it. Treat a drift level as an account of the evidence, not a measurement.

Compass reads your agents' session files and never writes to them. It never types into a session or chooses an answer for you; when a session asks through Compass, it returns the option you select. It keeps its own notes, your intent and a short history of what it observed, on your machine. With Compass on its default local address, session content leaves your machine only through model calls: Analyze drift, session summaries, Live monitor, and checks Compass runs on its own. Calls run when you press a control or enable a feature. Opening a finished Claude Code session can start a missing summary, with summaries enabled and within its limits. The first of each kind tells you what it sends and where. Pause model calls stops all of them, and --no-observer-model refuses them for a whole run. Compass also reads your Claude Code and Cursor quota, which sends no session content; turn it off on the Sessions screen or with --no-usage.

docs.title: With Workflow
docs.text: If you run work through Spacedock Workflow, Compass also shows which step each work item is in and the decisions Workflow recorded for it. It can alert you once when an item reaches a step you pick.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You run more than one agent session and cannot watch them all.
  • You step away during long runs and want to know, on return, which sessions need you.
  • Your review comments keep saying "this isn't what we agreed".

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Set your first intent. Install Spacedock, then state an intent for a session and check it for drift.
  • Then Workflow. If drift keeps coming from work that was never pinned down, Spacedock Workflow lets you write down once what good looks like at each step.
  • Compass reference: commands, options and keys.

docs.title: Start and stop
docs.text:
Command What it does Default /spacedock:compass Starts Compass from Claude Code. Port 4553 $spacedock:compass Starts Compass from Codex. Port 4553 spacedock compass --daemon Starts Compass in the background. Without --daemon it runs in the foreground. Foreground spacedock compass --status Says whether Compass is running on the port. Port 4553 spacedock compass --stop Stops Compass on the port. Port 4553 spacedock compass --diagnose Lists where Compass looks for each tool's sessions and whether it can read them. Starts nothing. --json prints it as JSON. Off spacedock compass --forget Deletes observation history, recorded session ends, stored session summaries and copied-correction records. Pauses model calls and turns summaries off until you turn them back on in the page. Keeps the goals you typed. Refused while Compass is running on the port. Off spacedock compass --version Prints the Compass version. Off spacedock compass --sessions [waiting] Lists running and recently finished sessions; with waiting, lists only sessions waiting on you, excluding the calling Claude Code session. Needs a running Compass instance. No waiting filter spacedock compass --footer Prints a Claude Code status-line segment from its input and Compass's saved state. Sends no request. May be used alone or with --session. Silent when nothing can be reported spacedock compass --help Prints the installed Compass options, including three experimental terminal and frontend development options omitted here. Off 
spacedock compass --port 4581 --daemon
spacedock compass --port 4581 --status
spacedock compass --port 4581 --stop

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Server options apply to the run you start. Stop and restart Compass to change one. Spell each option in full: an abbreviation is refused.

Option What it does Default --port PORT Port to serve on. Also selects the instance for --status, --stop and --forget. 4553 --window-hours HOURS Hides sessions with no activity in this window. 24 --unasked-readings Checks eligible sessions with a typed goal for drift without being asked, and raises departures only. Claude Code runs the check, except on Codex sessions, which Codex checks. If one CLI is not installed, the other checks instead. Codex needs permission first, for the destination shown in the Drift card. A goal saved unchanged from /goal, Use your prompt or a prompt draft is not checked. Spends model capacity: at most three checks per session and twelve a day. Off --session HARNESS:SESSION_ID Selects the session for --footer, for example claude:SESSION_ID. Used only with --footer. Status-line session ID, then CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID --claude-reading-model MODEL Claude model that reads a Claude Code session when you press Analyze drift. Takes an explicit Sonnet or Opus ID of generation 5 or later. claude-sonnet-5-5 --claude-monitor-model MODEL Claude model that Live monitor asks about once a minute. Takes an explicit Haiku ID of generation 4 or later. claude-haiku-5-5 --no-observer-model, --no-harness-usage Refuse every model call for the run, including Analyze drift, Find goal, summaries, Live monitor and unasked checks. Pause model calls in the page does the same until you resume. Off --no-annotations Does not read or save goals or outcome lines. Analyze drift stays visible and disabled. Off --no-git Does not run the end-of-session git check in your repositories. Off --no-ci-read Does not read pull-request or merge-request checks from GitHub or GitLab when you press Analyze drift. Off --no-focus Does not raise a session's terminal or record terminal identities. Off --no-dismiss Does not read or write the store of sessions marked handled. Off --no-ask Stops sessions from asking you questions through Compass. Off --no-events Stops the event coordinator, so state comes from scanning session files on a timer. Off --no-irreversible Stops reporting of risky command shapes such as force push and hard reset. Off --reach-url URL Webhook that receives counts-only nudges when sessions need input while you are away. None --no-reach Refuses off-machine nudges whatever URL is configured. Off --history-max-bytes BYTES Size cap on the history file, also its read cap. 1048576 --history-days DAYS Days of observed history to keep. 14 --no-history Does not read or write observed history. Off --no-spacedock Does not read Workflow definitions, so stage strips are not shown. Off --no-tripwires Does not read or save stage alerts. Off --quiet-hours WINDOW Silences non-question notifications, including unasked-check notifications and stage alerts, in a local window such as 22:00-08:00. Unasked model checks still run. None --no-quiet-hours Ignores any configured quiet hours. Off --no-usage Does not read Claude Code and Cursor quota from the vendor for the run. Quota is read otherwise, and sends no session content. Turn off under the quota windows on the Sessions screen stops it from the page. Off --host ADDRESS 127.0.0.1, or 0.0.0.0 to serve every network interface with no authentication. Prefer an SSH tunnel. 127.0.0.1 --observer-model, --allow-tool-output Accepted but do nothing; will be removed in a later release. Off 
spacedock compass --port 4581 --window-hours 6 --no-observer-model
spacedock compass --port 4581 --daemon --unasked-readings --quiet-hours 22:00-08:00
spacedock compass --port 4581 --no-annotations --no-history
spacedock compass --port 4581 --daemon --reach-url https://ntfy.sh/my-topic

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Variable Effect COMPASS_HOME Moves Compass's own state, logs and stores. Default: .compass under your home directory. Use the same value for start, stop, status and forget. COMPASS_REACH_URL Reach webhook when --reach-url is absent. COMPASS_QUIET_HOURS Quiet-hours window when --quiet-hours is absent.

docs.title: What works on each tool
docs.text:
Every session from the ten agent tools shows on the board. The rest depends on what each tool records.

Feature Claude Code Codex Pi Antigravity Other tools Session on the board ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Goal filled from /goal ✓ ✓ ✓ Goal drafted from your first prompt ✓ ✓ Outline of what the session has done ✓ ✓ Model-written summary ✓ Drift level ✓ ✓; checks need codex-cli 0.149+ ✓ Goal-met claim checked against the record ✓ ✓ Live monitor ✓ Steer back ✓ Unasked checks ✓ ✓; once you allow Codex ✓ ✓; reads your prompts only

docs.title: Drift levels
docs.text:
Shown after Analyze drift, and by Live monitor on Claude Code sessions. Live monitor's level, labelled Live monitor · Haiku, is Haiku's read of where the latest turns are heading. Until its check returns, or while it is paused or capped, the page shows an estimate from checks and written files, which does not read what your intent says. The meanings below are that estimate's and the analysis's.

Level Meaning None or low No recorded signal against your intent. Medium A check passed and files were written after it, a failed check was followed by writes, or the agent made a claim the record contradicts. For the live estimate, some writes outside the folders your intent names also contribute Medium. High A check still fails after your last message with no later write. For the live estimate, most writes outside the folders your intent names also count as High. Extreme Both High conditions hold. An analysis never reads Extreme. Not enough recorded yet Too little in the record to estimate, or a goal too vague to read the work against.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Does s Opens Sessions p Opens Projects a Opens Attention / Focuses session search on the Sessions screen Escape Returns from a session to where you opened it, and from any other view to Sessions

docs.title: Use Compass
docs.text:
State an intent for a session, read the board, and act when an agent drifts from it.

Install Spacedock, which includes Compass by default. Compass can also be installed and run on its own.

docs.title: Start Compass
docs.text:
Claude CodeCodexOther agents 
/spacedock:compass
$spacedock:compass

In Antigravity, any other tool, or with no agent at all, start Compass from a terminal:

spacedock compass --daemon

Start and stop options are in the reference.

In Claude Code and Codex you can also ask your agent to "open compass". Compass starts on your machine and gives you its address, http://127.0.0.1:4553/ by default. It does not open a browser for you, so open the address yourself.

New to Intent and drift? Open See a sample session (view only) above the Sessions list. It is an anonymized Claude Code session that drifted, with a summary of what it did, its reading and the correction Compass composed. Nothing in it is saved, sent or run.

Some of what follows works on some agent tools only. What works on each tool lists which.

docs.title: Set the goal
docs.text:
1. Open the session. On the Sessions screen, click the session's row. Its page opens with an Intent card at the top.

  2. Give it a goal. Write what should be true when the work is done, in one box of up to 1,000 characters. There are four ways to fill it:

    • Type it.
    • Set /goal in the session. A /goal you set in Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity fills the box on its own, marked "From your /goal". A later /goal is offered beside your saved goal and never written over it.
    • Press Use your prompt to choose from up to five of your prompts. With nothing typed, Compass drafts the goal from your first prompt in a Claude Code or Codex session.
    • Press Find goal to have the model that runs Analyze drift look for a goal in the prompts you typed. It fills the box, marked Goal detected, only when your own words state a clear end state.

  3. Add the expected outcome, if you want. Open Expected outcome (optional) and add up to six lines of up to 240 characters, one check per line. With no lines, Compass reads the session against the goal's own end state.

  4. Press Save intent. Compass keeps the words and shows them beside the session from now on. Nothing is sent to the agent. Save typed or edited intent before analyzing. Analyze drift can adopt an untouched detected goal or prompt draft.

The goal came from the session's /goal. Below it, the Drift card shows that Claude Code marked the goal met, and asks about a later message that went beyond the goal.

docs.title: Read the board
docs.text:
Sessions puts active work first. Each active session answers four questions: where it is, what it is doing now, what it does next, and whether it is blocked. Your goal sits beside what the agent is doing, so a mismatch is visible without opening anything.

The Sessions screen opens with the link to the sample session, a count of active sessions, and one row for each active session showing its goal, what it is doing now, and whether it is blocked.

Open To see Sessions, key s Every session, active work first Projects, key p Sessions grouped by project. Each project opens to Now, Course, Decisions and Console Attention, key a What needs you: sessions waiting on a person, and sessions at risk Intent log Every session that has an intent, with what Compass raised about it. A link in the navigation, with no key

Press Escape in a session to go back.

docs.title: See what the session has done
docs.text:
Below Intent, What the session has done outlines a Claude Code or Codex session in short lines, one group per message you sent. Only the Claude Code outline includes the agent's replies, checks, failures and written folders. The outline uses no model.

On a Claude Code session the card also holds a summary written by a model: an opening paragraph on what the agent did, then phases you open one at a time. Each line cites the session entries it rests on, and a phase that holds evidence for a departure, or has failed tests, says so on its heading. A finished session is summarized when you open it. For a running one, press Summarize or Update summary.

Each summary line cites the entries it rests on. Phase headings flag the departures and failed tests inside them.

Turn off summaries stops them. Delete summary removes one session's summary; it takes two presses.

docs.title: Check a session for drift
docs.text:
1. Press Analyze drift on the session's Drift card. It runs on your press. The first time, Compass tells you what it sends and to which agent tool. A Claude Code session is read by Claude Code, or by Codex when claude is not installed. For a Claude Code session the analysis also sends the checks the session ran, the files it wrote and any pull request it created.

  2. Read the result. The card gives the drift level and the departures it found, or says it can't tell. Each departure is a card: What quotes the entries behind it, each with its number, such as [41], and Why Compass reads this as drift explains it. Hover a number to see that entry, or open it in Full activity at the bottom of the page. What the analysis read shows the model, your intent, the part of the session it read, and what it did not read.

The departure quotes each cited entry with its number and time, then says why Compass reads it as drift. Below it, a claim of the agent's that the record contradicts.

A session with a departure on record gets a Drift mark on the Sessions screen and moves up the list, below any session blocked on you.

When Claude Code or Codex says a /goal is met, the Drift card shows that as the harness's claim. Once you analyze, Compass says whether the session's record agrees with the claim, disputes it, or cannot confirm it. The claim never sets the drift level.

If the goal is too vague to read the work against, Analyze says so under the Goal field and shows no level. Rewrite the goal with what should be true when the work is done.

After a reading, the card offers Check again when new work or changed words came after it, and Analyze again when it is current.

Analyze drift reads recorded work from Claude Code, Codex and Pi sessions. Codex check evidence needs records from codex-cli 0.149 or later. On the other tools, the Drift card says Compass can't read work from that tool.

Each analysis uses model capacity from your Claude Code or Codex account. Compass allows 100 in a rolling twenty-four hours, shared across sessions and tools, and Find goal and failed attempts count. When the limit is spent, a banner at the top of the session page says when you can analyze again.

To stop model calls, press Pause model calls in Drift settings on the Drift card. It stops Analyze drift, summaries and Live monitor until you press Resume model calls.

docs.title: Watch a session live
docs.text:
For a Claude Code session, turn on Live monitor in Drift settings. While the page is open and its tab is visible, Compass asks Haiku through your Claude Code about once a minute where the latest turns are heading. It sends your saved goal and the recent turns, without tool output. The card and the page header show the level, None or low, Medium, High or Extreme, labelled Live monitor · Haiku, with one sentence on where the session is heading. Until a check returns, or while the monitor is paused or capped, they show an estimate from the session's checks and written files instead, with no model call.

Live monitor never notifies you and never shows on the Sessions screen. After 20 minutes it asks whether you still want it, and turns itself off if nobody answers within 10 minutes. It is not remembered across reloads. The levels are in the reference.

docs.title: Act on a departure
docs.text:
Compass never writes into your session. You choose what happens next.

If you gave the agent a direction after your intent, the Drift card quotes it ("Your 12:59 message adds:") and asks what it means for your intent:

  • Add as a line makes it an expected outcome line.
  • Make it the goal replaces your goal with it.
  • Leave it keeps your intent as it was.

Each choice waits for Save intent, except Leave it, which settles at once. Settle it before you analyze: while a later direction is unsettled, the reading may say it can't tell.

To correct the agent:

  1. Press Steer back. Compass composes a correction from your saved intent and the reading, under Correction to paste. Steer back is offered with a departure from your intent, on Claude Code sessions.

  2. Press Copy correction, and paste it into the session yourself. Compass never sends it.

The correction restates the goal, says where the session departed, and carries Compass's reason for each departure.

If a reading is wrong, press Mark as inaccurate. The analysis stops setting the drift level and Steer back, and nothing is sent or re-run. Press Undo to bring it back.

docs.title: Let Compass check while you are away
docs.text:
Compass can also check sessions with a typed goal without being asked, and raise only the departures. It spends model capacity with nobody watching, so it is off until you start Compass with the option:

spacedock compass --daemon --unasked-readings

Claude Code runs these checks with no further step, except on Codex sessions. Codex runs them on Codex sessions, and on any session when claude is not installed. Before Codex can run a check, turn on Allow Codex to run unasked checks in the session's Drift card; Attention points to it when sessions are waiting.

A goal saved unchanged from /goal, Use your prompt or a prompt draft is not checked; edit it or type your own, then press Save intent. A check reads your goal, not your outcome lines. On Antigravity it reads only the prompts you sent, so it can catch your own directions moving away from the goal, but not the agent's work. Unasked checks stop at three per session and twelve a day. What Compass raised shows on the session page under Raised while you were away, and in the Intent log.

docs.title: Get alerted when work reaches a step
docs.text:
With Workflow running, Compass can tell you once when a work item reaches a step you choose.

  1. Open the project from Projects, then its Course tab.

  2. Find Stage alerts, and choose a step. The list holds the steps your workflow declares.

  3. Press Save. The next time an item enters that step, Compass sends one notification. Items already in the step do not trigger it. Press Rearm to be alerted again.

Notifications are native on macOS, and browser notifications elsewhere while a Compass tab is open.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Compass reference: commands, options and keys.
  • Workflow. Spacedock Workflow keeps work moving through steps you define, and Compass shows where each item is.

docs.title: Gates and decisions
docs.text: A gate pauses work for a decision. You choose which stages need gates and what evidence each gate presents.

docs.title: Gate content
docs.text:
Gate content defines what you need to judge the work at that stage.

Decision Useful context and evidence Approve a plan Proposed behavior, alternatives and tradeoffs Accept an implementation Changes, test results and unresolved findings Release a change User impact, remaining risks and rollback plan

Ask your agent to adjust the gate content as you learn what helps you decide. The instructions live in the workflow README.

docs.title: Your decision
docs.text:
The agent presents the work, supporting evidence and a recommendation. You can respond in the conversation or use Spacedock Review.

Decision What happens next Approve The agent continues with the approved work Request changes The agent routes your feedback to the stage responsible for the changes Hold The agent pauses the work

The workflow records your decision and its reason.

docs.title: Rejections
docs.text:
A review stage can send failed work back for correction before it reaches you. The reviewer then checks the revised work.

The automatic correction loop stops after three cycles and asks you how to proceed.

docs.title: Delegation
docs.text:
You can explicitly authorize an agent to make specified decisions. State the scope and conditions of that authority in the conversation.

The agent still presents the evidence and records the decision under its own identity.

Related guides

  • Workflow operation
  • Review standards

docs.title: The operating model
docs.text: You define the goal, standards and decisions you retain. Your agent coordinates the work and brings those decisions to you with evidence.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Responsibility Captain You set the direction and make decisions, including what to delegate First officer Your coordinating agent assigns work, checks progress and presents decisions Ensign A worker agent performs a stage's work and reports the result

docs.title: Parallel work
docs.text:
A workflow can run several work items at once. Each item has its own progress record and decision points.

Ask your coordinating agent what needs attention, what is blocked or what can proceed.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
A separate review stage can check work against your standards. A gate brings you the evidence for the decision you retain.

Related guides

  • Workflow operation
  • Workflows and entities
  • Stage lifecycle

docs.title: The stage lifecycle
docs.text: Each work item moves through the stages in your workflow. Each stage defines the work to do and the evidence required.

docs.title: A development workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  design --> implementation --> review --> done
  review -. changes .-> implementation
  classDef gate stroke:#e3b04b,stroke-width:2.5px
  class design,review gate

In this example, the outlined stages pause for your decision: before implementation and after review.

Requested changes return to implementation. The reviewer checks the revised work before it returns to you.

docs.title: Stage settings
docs.text:
You can ask your agent to configure a stage to:

  • Pause at a gate.
  • Use a separate reviewer with fresh context.
  • Return findings to the stage responsible for corrections.
  • Limit concurrent work or use a specialist agent.

docs.title: Isolated work
docs.text:
Code stages can use separate Git worktrees so work items have their own branches and files.

Related guides

  • Workflow design
  • Gates and decisions

docs.title: Workflows and entities
docs.text: A workflow keeps its rules and work records as plain text in your repository. An entity is one work item.

docs.title: Workflow rules
docs.text:
The workflow README defines the stages, standards and gate content.

Ask your agent to change these rules as you learn what the work requires. You can also edit the README directly.

docs.title: Work items
docs.text:
Each work item has a Markdown record with its goal, acceptance criteria, progress and stage reports. Related artifacts can live beside it.

Your agent maintains the records as work proceeds. You can read them to understand what happened or resume in another session.

docs.title: State storage
docs.text:
Workflow state can live in a separate checkout to keep routine progress commits off your code branch.

Related guides

  • Workflow design
  • Frontmatter contract

docs.title: Your first workflow
docs.text: Install Spacedock, then describe a repeatable piece of work and decide where it needs your judgment.

docs.title: Describe the work
docs.text:
spacedock claude "/spacedock:commission ship features through design, implementation, and review"

The agent asks about your work and proposes a workflow. For example:

Each task moves through design, implementation and review.

You approve the design before implementation. A separate agent reviews the result before your final decision.

Requested changes return to implementation.

docs.title: Set the standards
docs.text:
Adjust the proposed stages, decision points and quality standards. Type review stages to walk through the standards with your agent.

For each decision point, specify the context and evidence you need. This is the workflow's gate content.

docs.title: Run the first tasks
docs.text:
Choose the first work items with your agent. After you accept the design and standards, the agent starts the work.

At a gate, the agent presents the evidence and asks for your decision. Approve, request changes or hold the work.

docs.title: Resume later
docs.text:
Run /spacedock:debrief before you end the session.

To resume:

spacedock claude

The agent reads the workflow records and picks up the work.

Related guides

  • Workflow operation
  • Project survey: start from your existing agent history.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Spacedock works with Claude Code and Codex.

docs.title: Install Spacedock
docs.text:
macOS with HomebrewLinux or macOS without Homebrew

brew trust spacedock-dev/tap brew install --cask spacedock-dev/tap/spacedock copy

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/main/install.sh | sh export PATH="${SPACEDOCK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH" copy

The installer looks up releases at spacedock.md with User-Agent spacedock-install/<version|unknown> (<os>; <arch>[; ci][; internal]). The version identifies the installed Spacedock binary. If the version probe fails or takes more than two seconds, the installer uses unknown. The installer uses GitHub directly if the route fails or takes more than five seconds.

PostHog counts each lookup without the caller's IP address. Plausible uses the caller's IP address to count the lookup but does not store it. CI lookups are not counted. The installer adds ; ci when CI is 1, true, yes, or on, regardless of case or surrounding whitespace. Set SPACEDOCK_INTERNAL=1 to add ; internal.

docs.title: Set up your agent
docs.text:
Claude CodeCodex

spacedock install --host claude copy

Run /reload-plugins or start a new session.

spacedock install --host codex copy

Start a new session.

docs.title: Confirm setup
docs.text:
spacedock doctor copy

In Codex, run spacedock doctor --host codex. Follow the instructions in the doctor output.

docs.title: Keep it up to date
docs.text:
Run spacedock update. It updates Spacedock, Review, Compass and their plugins together. A Homebrew install prints the brew upgrade command to run instead.

Your first review.

docs.title: Project survey
docs.text: Survey reads your local agent history to identify recurring work and decisions that need your attention.

docs.title: Survey the project
docs.text:
In Claude Code, run:

/spacedock:survey

Survey uses agentsview, a tool for reading agent session history. It asks before installing a missing dependency.

The survey is read-only. It reports:

  • Repeated work and manual interventions.
  • Current workstreams.
  • Unresolved decisions.

docs.title: Use the findings
docs.text:
Your agent can propose a workflow from the findings. You decide whether to create it and which decisions remain yours.

To describe a workflow yourself, see Your first workflow.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: Run spacedock <command> --help for the full options. Run spacedock for the command list.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: spacedock --version reports the version, platform and release channel. Inside an agent session, it also reports the runtime and sandbox.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
Command Agent spacedock claude Claude Code spacedock codex Codex spacedock pi Pi

Claude Code is the primary Workflow host. Codex and Pi support is experimental.

Launch from your project directory. You can include a task:

spacedock claude "continue the workflow"

Put agent-specific options after --. See Supported sandboxes for sandbox options and Local plugin development for local checkouts.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Command Purpose spacedock install Install or refresh the agent integration spacedock doctor Check installation and compatibility spacedock update Update Spacedock, Review, Compass and their plugins to the newest release on this binary's channel

install and doctor accept --host claude, --host codex or --host pi. The default is Claude Code. Follow the doctor output to resolve setup problems.

See Installation for the manual setup path.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Your agent uses these commands to operate the workflow.

Command Purpose spacedock status Read or update work item state spacedock new Create a work item spacedock dispatch Prepare worker assignments spacedock gate Prepare reviews, record decisions and read gate history spacedock merge guard Complete delivery and record the outcome spacedock state Manage the workflow state checkout spacedock completion Generate shell completions

spacedock gate read <ref-or-path> --json returns the stored gates object, including every attempt and its application state. References and paths use the same resolution as status --read, including archived entities. The command changes no files. Records and attempts retain their stored order. Scalar values retain their stored values. An entity without gate history returns {"records":[],"version":1}. Invalid gate data exits nonzero without JSON output.

spacedock gate read gate-history-json-reader --json --workflow-dir docs/dev
spacedock gate read archive:finished-task --json --workflow-dir docs/dev

See Workflow operation for the conversation you use to direct the work.

docs.title: Frontmatter contract
docs.text:
YAML frontmatter stores workflow settings and work item state. Your agent maintains these fields.

Record Contents Schema Workflow README Stages, defaults and decision points Workflow schema Work item Identity, current stage and outcome Entity schema

The schemas define field names, types and required values. Workflows and entities explains the files you see.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Stages, standards and decision points for a recurring type of work. See Workflows and entities.

docs.title: Entity
docs.text: One work item and its progress record. See Workflows and entities.

docs.title: Stage
docs.text: A step with defined work and standards, such as design, implementation or review. See Stage lifecycle.

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: A checkpoint that requires a decision before work continues. See Gates and decisions.

docs.title: Gate content
docs.text: The context and evidence presented at a decision point. See Gate content.

docs.title: First officer
docs.text: The agent that coordinates workers and brings decisions to you. See The operating model.

docs.title: Ensign
docs.text: A worker agent assigned to a stage. See The operating model.

docs.title: Mod
docs.text: An extension that adds workflow behavior without adding a stage. See Mods and standing teammates.

docs.title: Standing teammate
docs.text: A specialist agent available throughout a session. See Mods and standing teammates.

docs.title: Split-root state
docs.text: Workflow records stored in a separate Git checkout from the code. See Split-root state.

docs.title: Supported sandboxes
docs.text: Sandbox Platforms Trigger safehouse macOS A .safehouse profile in the working directory, --safehouse, or any --safehouse-* option

docs.title: Additional profiles
docs.text:
Option Type Description Default --safehouse-append-profile PATH Optional, repeatable path Append a safehouse policy file for this launch. None 
spacedock claude --safehouse-append-profile=file.sb
spacedock codex --safehouse-append-profile="profiles/local rules.sb"
spacedock pi --safehouse-append-profile=first.sb --safehouse-append-profile=second.sb

Both --safehouse-append-profile=PATH and --safehouse-append-profile PATH select safehouse. Place the option before --; tokens after -- go to the coding agent. Relative paths start in the directory where you launch Spacedock. Each occurrence supplies one path; repeats retain their order. Safehouse loads project-config profiles before these profiles, then applies its final write protections. Safehouse reports invalid profile paths or content, and Spacedock returns the failure. An existing sandbox stays active; this option still requests a safehouse launch and cannot relax the parent sandbox.

docs.title: Spacedock Review
docs.text: More agent work means more decisions for you. Review plans, drafts and reports, then decide what happens next.

docs.title: Your decision
docs.text:
Select text to leave a comment, then make the call:

  • Approve: the agent can proceed.
  • Request changes: ask the agent to revise.
  • Hold decision: pause the work.

Your agent picks up your feedback and acts on your decision. No need to copy it back into the conversation.

docs.title: Local and hosted
docs.text:
TerminalBrowser

Review beside your agent. The document stays on your machine. Leave comments and approve, request changes or hold the work.

Supported terminals and controls

review.spacedock.md is Spacedock’s hosted review service, free with limits. Create an account and pair your computer for higher limits.

People you invite can comment through the link you share with them.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Each agent that asked for a review waits for its own result, the way its tool (Claude Code or Codex) waits.

When you finish, the result contains your decision, anchored comments and the document version you reviewed, and it goes back to the conversation that asked. Claude Code and Codex wait differently, but receive the same result.

Related guides

  • Your first review: send your own plan, leave feedback and read the agent’s response.
  • Comments and decisions: what each decision means.
  • Sharing: invite others before you make the call.
  • Spacedock Workflow: define what needs your judgement and what evidence each review presents.

docs.title: Browser review
docs.text: Review your agent’s work in your browser. Spacedock hosts the uploaded document; your agent stays in its existing environment.

docs.title: Open your review
docs.text:
In Claude Code, request a decision in the browser:

/spacedock:review plan.md web decision copy

In Codex, use $spacedock:review with the same arguments.

Or ask your agent:

Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review in the browser for a decision.

Agree to the upload. The first time, your agent runs subspace-relay-client pair for you to pair this computer with your account: sign in and approve in the browser page it opens. You pair once per computer.

Over SSH, the terminal shows a link and a code instead. Open the link in a browser on any device, sign in, enter the code and approve. Then confirm in the terminal: answer y. If your agent started the pairing and reports paired: not yet, run subspace-relay-client pair --confirm in your own terminal on that computer and answer y there.

Your agent then opens the review. Signed in, you are the owner and make the decision. Send the same share link to invite others; they comment, and only you decide.

docs.title: Comment and decide
docs.text:
1. Select text and add a comment.
  2. Press Finish review. Choose Approve, Request changes or Hold decision.
  3. Press Send decision. Your agent receives the decision and included comments. The review closes.

Comments you have added are included automatically; add or cancel any text still in the comment box first. For comments already sent, select Include beside each one you want returned with your decision.

To send comments while keeping the review open, choose Send comments, leave open. You can decide later.

Related guides

  • Sharing
  • Comments and decisions
  • Link expiry and waiting limits

docs.title: Comments and decisions
docs.text:
A comment identifies something to discuss or change. A decision tells your agent whether to continue, revise or stop.

Decision What happens next Approve The agent continues the task within the permission you already gave it Request changes In the browser, the agent revises the file using your feedback and shares it again. In the terminal, the agent receives your feedback and acts within the permission it already has Hold decision The agent pauses the work

A decision closes the review. Comments alone do not mean approval.

Your decision can include comments. In a shared review, invited reviewers can comment. Only you, as the owner, make the decision.

Related guides

  • Terminal decisions
  • Browser decisions
  • Workflow gates

docs.title: Review requests
docs.text:
Use /spacedock:review in Claude Code or $spacedock:review in Codex. Both use the same arguments. Replace plan.md with your file name.

Arguments What happens plan.md terminal decision Review in the terminal and make a decision plan.md web decision Review in the browser and make a decision, after agreeing to the upload plan.md decision Make a decision using your project's saved review location plan.md terminal questions Review in the terminal with questions enabled plan.md Review the file using your project's saved location terminal Save Terminal as this project's preference web Save Web as this project's preference, after agreeing to uploads No arguments View or change this project's preference A prompt, such as draft release notes for v2 Ask the agent to carry it out, then review the resulting file

A location supplied with a file applies to that review only. Without a saved preference, your agent asks where to review.

To save a preference, terminal also accepts tui or local, and web also accepts webui or remote. With a file, use terminal or web exactly.

Or ask your agent:

Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review for a decision.

docs.title: Terminal keys
docs.text: Key Action c Comment on selected text s Suggest replacement text Q Ask the agent a question when questions are enabled R Refresh the answer to your latest question T Set an automatic answer refresh interval; press again to stop q Finish, or open the decision screen Tab Choose a decision on the finish screen Enter Send the decision, or save the note you are editing Esc Leave the finish screen, or discard the note you are editing ? Show all keys

docs.title: Review modes
docs.text:
Mode Result feedback Comments binding Comments and the owner's decision

A plain terminal file review defaults to feedback. The decision keyword requests binding mode.

Your agent receives approve, revise or hold for Approve, Request changes and Hold decision. See Comments and decisions for what each means.

docs.title: Agent commands
docs.text:
Installing Spacedock adds subspace-relay-client; a Homebrew install also names it rr, which the table uses. After a curl install, type subspace-relay-client in place of rr. Your agent runs these for you.

Command Action rr pair Pair this computer with your account, once; you sign in and approve in your browser rr publish <file> --open Upload the file, print its share link and open it in your browser rr decision <share-url> --with-included Wait for the owner's decision and included comments rr feedback <share-url> Read the review's comments and decisions from the publishing machine rr revoke <share-url> Revoke access through the share link rr device Check whether this computer is paired with an account rr unpair Unpair this computer. Share links keep working; you decide on its reviews again after pairing

Use --timeout with rr decision to set the wait duration, for example --timeout 110m.

Your paired computers are listed at review.spacedock.md/account/computers, where you can remove one.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value Share link Seven days from sharing by default Automatic wait in Claude Code Up to 110 minutes Automatic wait in Codex Up to 12 hours Shares per day, unpaired computer 5 Shares per day, paired computer 100 per computer and 100 across the account's computers File size 1 MB per share Feedback sends 100 per reviewer session, 200 per review

docs.title: Shared reviews
docs.text: Invite others to comment before you decide. Send them the share link from your browser review; they comment, and only you decide.

docs.title: Reviewer access
docs.text:
Reviewers open the link, select text and comment. They need nothing installed and can use an anonymous name or sign in.

You see everyone’s comments. Each reviewer sees only their own. A reviewer can also give the link to their agent to leave feedback; it reads review.spacedock.md/llms.txt and comments under the name it declares.

docs.title: Make the call
docs.text:
Signed in as the owner, select Include beside the comments you want your agent to receive. Then send your decision.

Only the owner decides. Finishing with a decision closes the review to further comments.

docs.title: Document access
docs.text:
Spacedock’s hosted service stores the uploaded document, comments and decision. Anyone holding the share link can read the entire document, so share it only with people who should have access.

Share links expire after seven days by default. Review the limits and create an account and pair your computer for higher limits. Ask your agent to revoke the link to end access sooner. For example: "Revoke the share link for plan.md."

Related guides

  • Browser review
  • Link and account limits

docs.title: Terminal review
docs.text: Review beside your agent in tmux, Zellij, Herdr or cmux, or in a Ghostty or Apple Terminal window. The file stays on your machine.

docs.title: Open the review
docs.text:
In Claude Code, request a decision in the terminal:

/spacedock:review plan.md terminal decision copy

In Codex, use $spacedock:review with the same arguments.

terminal is optional. Omit it to use your project's saved preference. To save Terminal for this project, run /spacedock:review terminal.

Or ask your agent:

Open plan.md in Spacedock Review in the terminal and ask for my decision.

docs.title: Comment or suggest an edit
docs.text: Select text, then press c to comment or s to suggest replacement text.

docs.title: Finish the review
docs.text:
Press q to open the finish screen. Press Tab to choose Approve, Request changes or Hold decision, then Enter to send.

Request changes and Hold decision need a comment, a suggested edit or an overall note. Your agent receives your decision and comments.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
In Claude Code, open the terminal review with questions enabled:

/spacedock:review plan.md terminal questions copy

Or ask your agent:

Open plan.md in Spacedock Review in the terminal with questions enabled.

Answers appear beside the document and use the agent's original conversation context.

Press Q to ask a question, such as "What's next?"

Press T, enter an interval in minutes, then Enter to refresh the answer automatically. Press T again to stop.

Related guides

  • Comments and decisions
  • Terminal keys
  • Workflow gates

docs.title: Your first review
docs.text:
Install Spacedock. In Claude Code, use the review skill. Replace plan.md with your file name:

/spacedock:review plan.md decision copy

In Codex, use $spacedock:review with the same arguments.

Or ask your agent:

Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review for a decision.

No active plan right now? Try this:

Based on my recent agent history, draft a concise recommendation on whether we should adopt Spacedock Review. Use /spacedock:review to send it to me for a decision. copy

docs.title: Open the review
docs.text:
Choose Terminal to review on your machine, or Web to review in your browser. Your agent remembers the choice for this project.

For Web, agree to the upload the first time in a project. The first time on a computer, your agent runs subspace-relay-client pair for you to pair this computer with your account: sign in and approve in your browser. After that, your agent opens the review and you decide while signed in.

docs.title: Add a comment
docs.text:
Select the text you want changed.

  • Terminal: press c to add a comment.
  • Browser: type your comment in the box that opens.

docs.title: Finish the review
docs.text:
• Approve to let your agent continue.
  • Request changes to send the work back with your feedback.
TerminalBrowser

Press q to open the finish screen. Press Tab to choose your decision, then Enter to send.

Press Finish review, choose your decision, then Send decision.

Your agent receives your comments and decision automatically.

Related guides

  • Comments and decisions: what happens after your decision.
  • Terminal controls and approval requests
  • Browser review
  • Sharing

docs.title: Workflow design
docs.text: Describe the work to your agent. It proposes stages, standards and decision points for you to adjust.

docs.title: Describe the work
docs.text:
In a session started with spacedock claude, use:

/spacedock:commission ship features through design, implementation, and review

docs.title: Review the design
docs.text:
You decide:

  • The work items: what each task produces.
  • The stages: how each task moves from an idea to completion.
  • The decision points: where work pauses for you and where requested changes go.
  • The standards: what agents must produce and check at each stage.

For each decision point, gate content defines the context and evidence the agent presents to you.

docs.title: Refine the standards
docs.text: The generated rules are a starting point. Ask your agent to refine them, or type review stages for a walkthrough of each stage.

docs.title: Run the workflow
docs.text: After you accept the design and standards, the agent starts the first work items. Your first workflow shows the full interaction.

docs.title: Session debrief
docs.text: A debrief records completed work, decisions and follow-up items for the next session.

docs.title: Record the session
docs.text:
In Claude Code, run:

/spacedock:debrief

The agent drafts the record from Git history and workflow files. You confirm the session's scope and add context behind decisions.

docs.title: Follow-up work
docs.text: Workflow improvements stay with the project. For Spacedock bugs, the agent offers to file an anonymized GitHub issue. You approve or edit each issue before it sends it.

docs.title: Workflow operation
docs.text: Talk to your agent to add work, check progress and make decisions.

docs.title: Start a session
docs.text:
spacedock claude

The agent reads the workflow records and continues work that is ready. It coordinates workers and brings you decisions or blockers.

docs.title: Check progress
docs.text:
Ask questions such as:

  • What needs my decision?
  • What is blocked?
  • What is ready next?

You can add work or change priorities in the same conversation.

docs.title: Decide at a gate
docs.text:
The agent presents the evidence specified by the workflow's gate content. You can approve, request changes or hold the work.

Your decision and feedback become part of the work item's record. The agent continues or routes the requested changes according to the workflow.

docs.title: End a session
docs.text:
Run /spacedock:debrief to record the completed work, decisions and follow-up items.

The next session reads the workflow records to resume the work.

docs.title: Spacedock Workflow
docs.text: Your agents can do more work than you can review. Spacedock Workflow lets you define what needs your attention and what agents can handle themselves.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
A workflow gives recurring work a set of stages, such as design, implementation and review. You define the standards for each stage. Agents choose how to do the work within those standards.

You also choose where work pauses for your decision. These checkpoints are called gates.

The stages and standards live in plain text in your repository. Your agent coordinates the work and records its progress and decisions.

docs.title: Gate content
docs.text:
Different stages need different context and evidence for your judgment. Gate content defines what the agent presents at each decision point.

For example, a feature workflow can pause before implementation. The agent brings you the proposed behavior, tradeoffs and a recommendation. You approve the plan, request changes or hold the work.

After approval, agents can implement and review the change against your standards. You can require another decision before release, with test results and unresolved risks as evidence.

Spacedock Review presents the work for your feedback and decision. Workflow defines when that review happens, what it contains and what happens next.

docs.title: Standards and trust
docs.text:
You and your agent can refine the standards and gate content as you learn what each decision needs. Add missing context, remove distracting detail, or change the evidence required.

You can also add decision points or explicitly delegate decisions to an agent. You control how much attention the workflow requires.

Related guides

  • Your first workflow: design a workflow and run its first work items.
  • Project survey: identify the process in your existing agent history.
  • Review standards: define what good work looks like at each stage.

docs.title: Review standards
docs.text:
Standards define what agents must produce and check at each stage. The rules generated during workflow design are a starting point.

Ask your agent to refine them, or type review stages during workflow design for a walkthrough.

Standards define good work. Gate content defines the evidence you see before a decision. You can refine both as the workflow develops.
